rules.rainArea: gauges whose nearest storm overflow monitor (within 15 km) is this company's; plain average of those with a full day's readings; no figure with fewer than 5
rules.hours: time inside the week; a monitor reporting one discharge for more than 72 hours straight is left out
rules.spills: counted the Environment Agency's way (12/24): the first 12 hours of discharges are one spill, then each further 24 hours with any discharge is one more; "discharges" is every separate on and off
rules.dryDay: a discharge that started on a day when the nearest gauge within 10 km recorded 0.25 mm or less that day and the day before; spills counted the EA's way; listed by monitor, with that gauge's readings for each day flagged; a flag to look at, not proof of a permit breach
rules.gaugeNames: rain gauges are named after their parish or district (nearest postcode, Postcodes.io)
rules.baseline: hours in the Environment Agency annual returns for the year, divided by 52
rules.sources: Spills: our record of the water companies' live storm overflow feeds (provisional). Rain: Environment Agency rainfall API (Open Government Licence v3). Baseline: Environment Agency Event Duration Monitoring annual returns.
